context: A 4-layer Sankey diagram mapping supply chain flow from 8 raw materials through 12 components and 8 products to 5 market regions, with animated particle flow on links and hover-to-trace interaction.
first_impression: Dense but navigable — the dark background and semi-transparent links manage the crossing complexity reasonably well at this scale.
what_works: The hover trace interaction (backward + forward BFS highlighting) is the right design choice for this density, progressively disclosing individual supply chains without overwhelming the viewer at rest. Four distinct color scales per layer clearly signal column identity and help the eye parse left-to-right directionality.
what_doesnt: The materials-to-components section has ~33 links crossing 8×12 node pairs at density 0.35, producing a tangle that is unreadable without hovering — structure (which materials dominate which components) cannot be extracted at a glance. Particle animation adds visual noise without encoding information; perceptual impact of up to 3000 simultaneous moving particles across all links cannot be assessed from a static screenshot but risks overwhelming the decorative-vs-signal balance.
